inclusion.I1: Empirical English language MRI studies assessing grey matter (GM) volume differences between substance users and controls
inclusion.I2: Any grey-matter structural measure qualifies- GM volume, GM density, GM concentration, and also surface-based measures such as cortical thickness or cortical volume. Do not exclude a study because its grey-matter measure is cortical thickness rather than voxel-based volume.
inclusion.I3: Any substance of abuse qualifies, not only alcohol, nicotine, opioids, cannabis and stimulants. Studies of other psychoactive substances (e.g. betel quid/areca nut, psychedelics) are in scope and must not be excluded for being outside a named list.

exclusion.E3: Studies in which a psychiatric or neurological PATIENT GROUP, rather than substance use, is the grouping variable (e.g. schizophrenia vs controls, epilepsy vs controls). Do NOT exclude a substance-user sample merely because its participants also carry a comorbid diagnosis such as ADHD, conduct disorder, antisocial personality or depression, which is the norm in this literature.

inclusion.I4: Empirical English language MRI studies assessing grey matter (GM) volume differences (e.g., volume, density, or concentration) between substance users and controls
inclusion.I5: Grey-matter measure- GM volume, density or concentration, and also surface-based measures such as cortical thickness or cortical volume. Do not exclude a study because its grey-matter measure is cortical thickness rather than voxel-based volume.
inclusion.I6: Whole-brain evidence- The paper must report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls comparing a grey-matter measure, computed as a voxelwise or vertexwise statistical map. A voxelwise map confined to a single anatomical sub-volume (e.g. a cerebellum-restricted SUIT analysis) still qualifies, provided it reports voxel coordinates.
inclusion.I7: Significant foci must exist- that whole-brain contrast must yield at least one SIGNIFICANT cluster with reported peak coordinates (x, y, z in MNI or Talairach space). A whole-brain contrast that the paper describes as null, non-significant, or yielding no surviving clusters does NOT satisfy this criterion, even though it was performed and reported, and even if significant findings are reported elsewhere from an ROI or small-volume-corrected analysis. This meta-analysis pools coordinates and a null contrast contributes none.
inclusion.I8: It is acceptable for qualifying voxelwise results to be reported in tables of coordinates, figures, or supplementary materials when the main text clearly indicates those results are available.
inclusion.I9: Reporting of participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software is preferred; missing one or more of these details alone should not exclude an otherwise qualifying study.

exclusion.E5: Studies that report only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results.
exclusion.E6: Studies whose only between-group result is derived from a predefined ATLAS PARCELLATION (per-region average volumes or thicknesses over atlas labels, e.g. AAL or FreeSurfer Desikan-Killiany regions) or from a MULTIVARIATE CLASSIFIER, rather than from a voxelwise or vertexwise statistical map. Whole-brain coverage by an atlas does not make a parcellation analysis a whole-brain voxelwise analysis; the source meta-analysis excludes region-of-interest analyses because they violate the ALE null hypothesis.
exclusion.E7: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses, methods-only, simulations) without original human structural MRI data.

inclusion.GLOBAL_I1: Voxelwise whole-brain grey matter comparison between substance users and controls, with a users < controls contrast indicating reduced grey matter in substance users.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I2: Must be a voxelwise whole brain analysis of grey matter volume
inclusion.GLOBAL_I3: Multiple experiments from the same article may be included only when they share the same control group but involve non-overlapping substance-user groups. For example, moderate smoker<control, and separately severe smoker<control include two different samples of cigarette smokers.

exclusion.GLOBAL_E1: Region of interest (ROI) or small volume correction (SVC) analyses
exclusion.GLOBAL_E2: Analyses other than substance users < controls (e.g., user > control contrasts)
exclusion.GLOBAL_E3: Analyses of other modalities (e.g., functional MRI, diffusion tensor imaging) or other structural measures

inclusion.ALL_DRUG_CLASSES_I1: Comparison of drug users of any class to controls

inclusion.ALCOHOL_I1: Comparison of alcohol users to controls

exclusion.ALCOHOL_E1: Comparison of users of other drug classes to controls

inclusion.NICOTINE_I1: Comparison of nicotine users to controls

exclusion.NICOTINE_E1: Comparison of users of other drug classes to controls

inclusion.OPIOIDS_I1: Comparison of opioid users to controls

exclusion.OPIOIDS_E1: Comparison of users of other drug classes to controls

inclusion.STIMULANTS_I1: Comparison of stimulant users to controls

exclusion.STIMULANTS_E1: Comparison of users of other drug classes to controls

inclusion.CANNABIS_I1: Comparison of cannabis users to controls

exclusion.CANNABIS_E1: Comparison of users of other drug classes to controls
